t.1.81.1: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Thus King Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, having consecrated his beloved son in the kingship, joyfully became a forest-dwelling hermit, a sage.
t.1.81.3: He went to that abode of the gods and dwelt there happily, rejoicing; but after no very great length of time he was cast down again by Śakra.
t.1.81.4: Fallen from heaven and falling, yet not having reached the surface of the earth, he then remained stationed in the midspace. Thus have I heard.
t.1.81.2: And how he, having made his dwelling in the forest, taking refuge there together with brahmins, living on fruits and roots and self-restrained, went from here to heaven.
t.1.81.5: And then from there, so tradition holds, the valiant one went again to heaven, together with King Vasumat and Aṣṭaka, having met, it is said, with Pratardana and Śibi in the assembly.
t.1.81.7: For Yayāti, lord of the earth, was equal to the king of the gods; he was the increaser of the Kuru lineage, with a splendor equal to that of fire.
t.1.81.6: By what deed did that lord of the earth attain heaven again? All of this I wish to hear in full and as it truly happened, told by you, O brahmin, in the presence of the hosts of brahmin seers.
t.1.81.8: I wish to hear in full the deeds of that great-souled one, whose fame was far-spread and whose renown was true, both in heaven and here on earth.
t.1.81.9: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Well then, I shall tell you the later story of Yayāti, which brings merit both in heaven and here on earth and destroys all sins.
t.1.81.10: King Yayāti, son of Nahuṣa, having consecrated his younger son Pūru in the kingship, then joyfully departed for the forest.
t.1.81.11: Having placed his sons, with Yadu at their head, in the border regions, the king lived for a long time in the forest, eating fruits and roots.
t.1.81.12: With his self disciplined and his anger conquered, satisfying the ancestors and the gods, and offering oblations into the fires according to rule, in keeping with the ordinance for forest-dwellers.
t.1.81.13: The mighty lord honored his guests with oblations of forest produce, and, adopting the way of life of gleaning grains, he made his meal of the food that remained.
t.1.81.14: For a full thousand years that king lived in this manner; for thirty autumns he subsisted on water alone, with speech and mind restrained.
t.1.81.15: And then, unwearied, he lived on air alone for a year; and the king practiced austerities for a year in the midst of five fires.
t.1.81.16: For six months he stood on one foot, living on air; then he of holy fame went to heaven, having filled both heaven and earth.
